user_profile.other_preferences: prepare for global market,Need a fast job, Intermediate (Built small projects) Coding experience, familiar with typescript, java,C,C++,PHP, javascript languages and familiar with node.js,React,.NET framewrok. Also build some academic project

prompt_used:
I want to become a Machine Learning Engineer. I have 2 months to prepare and I can study 1 hours per day. 
My experience level is University Recent CSE Graduate. prepare for global market,Need a fast job, Intermediate (Built small projects) Coding experience, familiar with typescript, java,C,C++,PHP, javascript languages and familiar with node.js,React,.NET framewrok. Also build some academic project
Now generate a learning plan for me.

generated_plan.title: 2-Month Machine Learning Engineer Learning Plan
generated_plan.goal: Prepare for a fast job in the global market as an ML Engineer with 1 hour/day study time.
prerequisites: Familiar with various programming languages (TypeScript, Java, C, C++, PHP, JavaScript)
generated_plan.study_commitment: 1 hour per day for 2 months (approx. 60 hours total)
focus_areas: ML Interview Prep & System Design Fundamentals

weeks_1_2.theme: Python for Data Science & Math Refresher
topics: Python Crash Course (syntax, data types, control flow, functions, basic OOP) - Allocate 2 hours
NumPy for numerical computation (arrays, operations, broadcasting) - Allocate 2 hours
Pandas for data manipulation (DataFrames, Series, I/O, basic operations) - Allocate 3 hours
Math Refresher: Linear Algebra (vectors, matrices, dot products, relevance to ML) - Allocate 3 hours
Math Refresher: Calculus (derivatives, gradients, chain rule intuition) & Probability (basic concepts, distributions) - Allocate 4 hours
suggested_resources: Codecademy/W3Schools Python for beginners (for quick syntax review)
Khan Academy: Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability & Statistics (focus on intuition)

topics: ML Concepts: Supervised/Unsupervised Learning, Regression/Classification, Bias-Variance Tradeoff, Overfitting/Underfitting - Allocate 2 hours
Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Pandas & Matplotlib/Seaborn - Allocate 3 hours
Data Preprocessing: Handling missing values, categorical encoding, feature scaling - Allocate 2 hours
Linear Regression: Theory, implementation with Scikit-learn, evaluation metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE, R-squared) - Allocate 3 hours
Logistic Regression: Theory, implementation with Scikit-learn, evaluation metrics (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC) - Allocate 2 hours
Decision Trees & Random Forests: Basic theory, Scikit-learn implementation - Allocate 2 hours
suggested_resources: Andrew Ng's Machine Learning Course (Coursera - focus on conceptual lectures)
'Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras & TensorFlow' (Geron) - specific chapters

weeks_5_6.theme: More ML Algorithms & Introduction to Deep Learning
topics: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) & Support Vector Machines (SVMs): Basic theory and Scikit-learn usage - Allocate 3 hours
Ensemble Methods: Gradient Boosting Machines (XGBoost/LightGBM) - high-level understanding and basic usage - Allocate 3 hours
Unsupervised Learning: K-Means Clustering (theory and Scikit-learn) - Allocate 1 hour
Introduction to Neural Networks: Perceptrons, Activation Functions, Feedforward NNs (conceptual understanding) - Allocate 3 hours
Deep Learning Framework (TensorFlow/Keras preferred): Install, build a simple sequential model for classification (e.g., MNIST) - Allocate 3 hours
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs): Conceptual understanding, when to use - Allocate 1 hour
suggested_resources: DeepLearning.AI Specialization (Coursera - first course, focus on concepts)

weeks_7_8.duration: 18 hours (9 hours/week, with buffer for catch-up)
topics: Mini-Project (End-to-end): Choose a small dataset (e.g., Kaggle Titanic, Housing Prices). Apply EDA, preprocessing, train 2-3 models, evaluate, interpret results. Focus on clear code and insights. - Allocate 6 hours

Data Structures & Algorithms (DS&A) for Interviews: Focus on common patterns (arrays, strings, hash maps, linked lists, basic trees). Solve 1-2 easy/medium LeetCode problems per day (in Python). - Allocate 6 hours
ML Interview Questions Review: Be ready to explain algorithms, evaluation metrics, bias-variance, regularization, feature engineering, common pitfalls. Discuss project choices. - Allocate 3 hours
ML System Design (Conceptual): Understand the components of an ML system (data ingestion, model training, inference, monitoring, re-training). How to approach design questions. - Allocate 2 hours
Resume/LinkedIn Optimization: Highlight new ML skills, projects, and relevant academic background. - Allocate 1 hour
suggested_resources: Glassdoor/Blind/YouTube (for common ML interview questions and system design examples)

important_notes: This plan is highly condensed. Focus on understanding concepts intuitively rather than memorizing formulas.
Leverage your existing strong programming background to quickly grasp Python syntax and programming paradigms.
Prioritize hands-on implementation over deep theoretical dives. Practical application solidifies understanding.
While you know many languages, Python is the industry standard for ML. Dedicate almost all coding practice to it.
For 'fast job' and 'global market', DS&A skills are critical even for ML roles. Don't skip this section.
Be prepared to demonstrate your project work effectively during interviews.
Consider the 'Intermediate' level for coding. If you feel comfortable, you might allocate more time to ML concepts/DS&A.
Network and look for entry-level/junior ML Engineer or Data Scientist roles, as 'ML Engineer' can be a broad title with varying expectations.
